identification.summary: Ruthless Rabbit is an Infoblox-named, financially motivated investment-scam actor that runs fake investment platforms and uses registered domain generation algorithms (RDGAs) to pre-register large numbers of domains [S1][S2]. It operates its own cloaking service that performs validation checks on visitors and filters out non-target traffic, which makes the scams harder to detect [S3]. It impersonates real local news sites and brands such as WhatsApp or Meta [S3]. Malpedia's entry, which repeats Infoblox findings, says the activity primarily targets Russia, Poland, Romania and Kazakhstan [S4]. This is a cybercrime cluster, not a state-sponsored actor.
identification.firstObserved: Malpedia states the actor has run investment scams since November 2022 [S4]. Infoblox says it discovered the actor in July 2024 and published in April 2025 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: The name is Infoblox's. No Microsoft name or MITRE group exists for this actor. Infoblox pairs it with a separate cluster, Reckless Rabbit, which uses Facebook ads with fake celebrity endorsements and wildcard DNS; Infoblox's VP of threat intelligence said the team would need to look closer before linking the two [S3]. Do not merge their facts. Several details below are known only from secondary coverage of Infoblox's report because the primary pages could not be opened in this session.

attribution.confidence: No state sponsor is asserted in the sources gathered. One secondary summary of the coverage says Infoblox researchers believe the actor appears linked to infrastructure in Russia; this was not confirmed against the primary report.
attribution.basis: Infoblox infrastructure and DNS analysis as relayed by secondary coverage [S1][S3][S4].

objectives: Financial gain by luring victims to fake investment platforms, including crypto exchanges, and collecting personal data through embedded web forms [S3].

regions: Russia, Poland, Romania and Kazakhstan (Malpedia, repeating Infoblox) [S4]
targeting.notes: Victims are consumers, not organizations. The country list comes from Malpedia and was not independently confirmed in the other sources [S4].

capabilities.summary: Uses RDGAs to pre-register thousands of short-lived domains so it can rotate them quickly [S2]. Malpedia cites over 2,600 domains on multiple dedicated IPs [S4]. Operates a cloaking service with validation checks, geofencing and wildcard DNS to show scam content only to valid targets and hide it from scanners [S2][S3]. Frequently changes landing-page URL paths to hinder tracing [S3]. Lures include spoofed local news articles and brand impersonation (WhatsApp, Meta) [S3]; Malpedia adds Baltic Pipe, Google Finance and a spoofed Channel One article promoting a 'GazInvest' platform [S4]. Secondary coverage ties the cloaking service to the domain mcraftdb.tech; this was not verified against the primary report.

diamond.adversary: Unnamed criminal operators tracked by Infoblox as Ruthless Rabbit; identity and sponsor unknown [S2].
diamond.capability: RDGA domain pre-registration, wildcard DNS, geofencing, own cloaking service, spoofed news and brand lures [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Thousands of rotating domains on multiple dedicated IPs (over 2,600 per Malpedia) and a cloaking service [S2][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven fraud exploiting trust in local news and well-known brands [S3].
diamond.technology: Reliance on DNS, which attackers exploit through RDGAs and wildcard responses, and on web forms that collect user data [S2][S3].

provenance.importedSummary: Ruthless Rabbit has been running investment scam campaigns since November 2022, primarily targeting users in Russia, Poland, Romania, and Kazakhstan. The actor utilizes RDGA patterns to create over 2,600 domains, hosted on multiple dedicated IPs, and employs a cloaking service for validation checks on user leads. Their campaigns have included themes such as Baltic Pipe financial scams and spoofing well-known platforms like WhatsApp and Google Finance. The most prevalent campaign theme involves a spoofed news article from "Channel One" promoting the "GazInvest" platform with promises of high returns.
